# Spoilage before the stall

Small growers around Lisbon pick in the early morning and reach the market by mid-morning. Leafy greens, soft fruit and herbs lose most of their shelf life in the hours between picking and the first sale, because nothing keeps them cool once the van is unloaded. Stall holders say a hot Saturday costs them a quarter of the table.

The loss is a cooling gap, not a supply gap: the produce is fine at the field and wilted by the afternoon.
